Went further: a **fixed five-year tenure for Governors** and removal only by **impeachment-like process by the state legislature**, appointment from a **panel prepared by the state**, **'localised' President's Rule** confined to a district or region rather than the whole state, a **Superintendence-free CBI requiring state consent**, and an amendment to Article 355 to define the Union's duty to protect states.

Set up by Tamil Nadu — the first substantial state-side critique: **abolish Articles 356, 357 and 365**, make the **Finance Commission a permanent body**, transfer subjects from the Union to the State List, and constitute an **Inter-State Council** at once. The founding document of the state-autonomy demand.

**15th FC (N.K. Singh)**: states' share **41%**, horizontal criteria — income distance 45%, area 15%, population (2011) 15%, demographic performance 12.5%, forest and ecology 10%, tax effort 2.5%; a separate **defence and internal security fund**. **16th FC (Arvind Panagariya)** reports for **2026-31** — its live questions are cesses and surcharges, the treatment of centrally sponsored schemes, and grants to local bodies.

On panchayati raj: recommended a **two-tier system (Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat)**, made the **Zila Parishad the pivot** of planning, allowed **open participation of political parties**, and proposed compulsory taxation powers and reservation for SC/ST. Its logic underlies the 73rd Amendment even though the two-tier design was not adopted.

Recommended **'democratic decentralisation'** and the **three-tier structure** — Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti (the executive body) and Zila Parishad (advisory and supervisory), with the **Block as the unit** and genuine transfer of resources. Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 October 1959) implemented it first, followed by Andhra Pradesh.

First to recommend **constitutional status for panchayati raj**, the **gram sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy**, **nyaya panchayats** for judicial functions, and **regular elections through a State Election Commission** — the intellectual blueprint of the 73rd Amendment.

On Telangana — examined six options and became the reference document for the **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014**. Pair with the **Fazl Ali States Reorganisation Commission (1955)** — which rejected language as the *sole* basis but produced the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** and 14 states plus 6 UTs — and the **Dhar Commission (1948)** and **JVP Committee (1949)**, which had opposed linguistic states.

**15 reports**. Signature recommendations: the **Right to Information as the master key to good governance** (1st), **Ethics in Governance** — a National Ombudsman, state funding of elections, partial disqualification on framing of charges (4th), **Local Governance** with 'a total transfer of functions, functionaries and funds' (6th), **Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution** (7th), a **Public Services Bill and a Central Civil Services Authority** (10th), and 'Refurbishing of Personnel Administration' (10th). The default citation for any governance reform answer.

items.t: First ARC (1966-70, Morarji Desai then K. Hanumanthaiya)
items.d: 20 reports; recommended **Lokpal and Lokayukta** (the origin of the idea in India), the creation of a **Department of Personnel** outside ministries, and specialisation in the civil services through mid-career streaming.

On the prevention of corruption — produced the **Central Vigilance Commission** and the vigilance-officer network, and identified the 'four-fold' sources of corruption in administrative delay, scarcity, cumbersome procedures and discretion.

On electoral reform: **state funding in kind**, **disqualification for booth capturing**, **a single election commission decision on disqualification under Art. 103/192 to follow the ECI's opinion**, restricting the anti-defection law to a vote of confidence and money bills, and the appointment of the CEC in consultation with the CJI and the Leader of Opposition.

On **state funding of elections** — recommended it **in kind and only for recognised parties and their candidates**, and only once **internal party democracy and audited accounts** are in place. Cite alongside the **Law Commission's 255th Report (2015)** on electoral reform and the **170th Report (1999)** on internal party democracy and the two-ballot system.

On the **criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus** — found that crime syndicates had developed a 'network of muscle-power, money-power and patronage' and had begun to enjoy political protection; recommended a nodal agency to collate intelligence. The founding official acknowledgement of criminalisation of politics.

On **'One Nation, One Election'** — recommended simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in the **first step**, and local body elections **within 100 days** in the second; a **single electoral roll and single voter ID**; and constitutional amendments to Articles 82A, 83, 172 and 324A, some requiring **state ratification**. Objections: federalism, the fate of a House that falls mid-term, and the national-issue dominance over state issues.

items.t: T.S.R. Subramanian Committee (2013 judgment; 2016 education committee)
items.d: The **service-reform directions** (Civil Services Board, fixed tenure, written orders) came from the Supreme Court in *T.S.R. Subramanian*. The **separate T.S.R. Subramanian Committee (2016)** on the New Education Policy preceded the **K. Kasturirangan Committee (2019)**, whose draft became **NEP 2020**.

Constituted after the December 2012 Delhi gang rape, reported in **29 days**: widened the definition of rape, recommended criminalising **marital rape** (not accepted), **stalking, voyeurism and acid attacks** as offences, punishment for **police failure to register an FIR**, and rejected the death penalty and lowering the juvenile age. Produced the **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013**.

items.t: Punchhi and Malimath on criminal justice
items.d: The **Malimath Committee (2003)** recommended shifting from adversarial towards a **partly inquisitorial** system, a lower standard of proof ('clear and convincing'), a **victim's right to participate and to compensation**, and a National Judicial Commission. The **Madhav Menon Committee (2007)** drafted the National Policy on Criminal Justice.

On the social, economic and educational status of Muslims — found their conditions **below the national average and in some respects below SC/STs**, coined the phrase that Muslims carry a 'double burden of being labelled anti-national and appeased'; recommended an **Equal Opportunity Commission**, a **Diversity Index** and a **National Data Bank**. Follow-up: **Ranganath Misra Commission (2007)** recommended 15% reservation for minorities (10% for Muslims) — not implemented.

Examined **sub-categorisation of OBCs** under Article 340; found that about **97% of central OBC quota benefits went to just 25% of OBC castes**, and nearly **10% of the sub-castes got nothing at all**. Recommended splitting the 27% into sub-quotas. Report submitted in 2023, not yet made public — the parallel to *Davinder Singh* on SC sub-classification.

Second Backward Classes Commission (**B.P. Mandal**) — identified **3,743 castes** as OBC, estimated them at **52% of the population**, and recommended **27% reservation**, implemented in 1990 and upheld in *Indra Sawhney*. Preceded by the **Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953)**, the first Backward Classes Commission, whose report was not acted upon.

The blueprint of India's public health system — recommended **integration of preventive and curative services**, a **three-tier structure with primary health centres**, and 'no individual should fail to secure adequate medical care because of inability to pay'. The ancestor of PHCs, and of the National Health Mission.

items.t: National Commission on Population and the health committees
items.d: Health policy lineage: **Bhore (1946)** → **Mudaliar (1962, quality over expansion)** → **Srivastava (1975, community health workers → the ASHA idea)** → **National Health Policy 1983, 2002 and 2017**. NHP 2017's targets: **public health spending 2.5% of GDP by 2025**, life expectancy 70 by 2025, and 'Health and Wellness Centres' — now **Ayushman Arogya Mandirs**.

**University Education Commission (Radhakrishnan, 1948)**; **Secondary Education Commission (Mudaliar, 1952)**; **Kothari Commission (1964-66)** — the **10+2+3 structure**, the **common school system**, the **three-language formula** and **6% of GDP for education**; **National Policy on Education 1968 and 1986** (with the 1992 Programme of Action); **NEP 2020** — 5+3+3+3+4 structure, GER 50% by 2035, multidisciplinary institutions, **HECI as a single regulator with four verticals**, and mother-tongue instruction till at least Class 5.

**FSLRC (Justice B.N. Srikrishna, 2013)** — recommended a unified **Financial Sector Regulatory Framework**, a single **Financial Redress Agency**, and merging regulators; **Narasimham Committees (1991, 1998)** on banking reform; **P.J. Nayak Committee (2014)** on bank board governance and the **Banks Board Bureau**; **Damodaran Committee (2011)** on customer service.

sections.h: Schemes and Missions — Target, Design, Number

items.t: AB PM-JAY — Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
items.d: **Target group**: bottom 40% — about 12 crore families / 55 crore people, extended in 2024 to **all citizens aged 70 and above** irrespective of income (~6 crore elderly). **Cover**: ₹5 lakh per family per year, secondary and tertiary care, cashless and portable across states, no cap on family size or age. **Numbers**: 8+ crore hospital admissions authorised, 30,000+ empanelled hospitals, ~₹1.2 lakh crore of authorised amount. **Critique**: CAG flagged invalid beneficiary IDs; outpatient care — the bulk of out-of-pocket spending — is excluded.

The renamed **Health and Wellness Centres** — over **1.75 lakh** upgraded sub-centres and PHCs delivering **12 packages of comprehensive primary care**, including NCD screening, mental health, elderly and palliative care, staffed by a **Community Health Officer** under a mid-level provider model. The preventive limb of Ayushman Bharat.

items.t: PM-ABHIM and the digital health stack
items.d: **PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission** — ₹64,180 crore for critical care blocks, block public health units, integrated public health labs and a **National Institution for One Health**. Alongside, **ABDM (Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission)** — **ABHA health IDs** (70+ crore created), a Health Professionals Registry and a Health Facility Registry, building the federated health-records architecture.

**PMBJP** — 15,000+ Janaushadhi Kendras selling generics at **50-90% below branded prices**, with cumulative savings to citizens of ~₹30,000 crore. Complemented by the **NPPA's** price capping of scheduled drugs, stents and knee implants under the **DPCO, 2013**.

**Mission Poshan 2.0** merges Anganwadi services, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls, using the **Poshan Tracker** to monitor 10 crore beneficiaries in real time; **PMMVY** gives **₹5,000** for the first live birth (and ₹6,000 for a second child if a girl); **JSY and JSSK** cover institutional delivery and free entitlements. Anaemia Mukt Bharat runs the 6x6x6 strategy.

**Samagra Shiksha** merges SSA, RMSA and teacher education into a single pre-school-to-Class-12 programme. **PM SHRI** upgrades **14,500 schools** as exemplar NEP-model schools. **PM POSHAN** (renamed mid-day meal) covers **11.8 crore children** in classes 1-8 — the world's largest school feeding programme, with roots in the Tamil Nadu scheme of 1962 and the Supreme Court's **PUCL (2001)** order that made it universal.

**National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy** — universal **foundational literacy and numeracy by Class 3**, with Lakshyas (learning outcome targets) for each stage and a five-tier implementation structure. Anchored in NEP 2020's finding that over 5 crore children lack foundational skills.

**PMKVY 4.0** with short-term training, on-job training and recognition of prior learning; the **National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme** and the new **PM Internship Scheme** targeting **1 crore internships in the top 500 companies over five years** with a monthly stipend. India's formally skilled workforce is still ~4-5% — the gap the schemes address.

The adult education scheme (2022-27) targeting **5 crore non-literates aged 15+** in foundational literacy, critical life skills, vocational skills and continuing education, delivered largely through **volunteerism**. India's literacy rate was 77.7% (NSO 2017-18), with the female rate ~70%.

groups.g: Welfare, social security and the vulnerable

items.t: PMGKAY — Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
items.d: **Free foodgrain to ~80 crore NFSA beneficiaries**, extended for five years from January 2024 at a cost of about **₹11.8 lakh crore**. Subsumes the NFSA entitlement rather than adding to it. Delivered through **One Nation One Ration Card** portability and e-PoS-enabled fair price shops.

**PM Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (2023)** — ₹24,104 crore for **75 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups** across 11 interventions (housing, road, water, electricity, mobile medical units, hostels). **Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (2024)** — ₹79,156 crore for **63,000 tribal-majority villages**, covering 5 crore tribal people. The largest tribal-focused outlays yet.

**Atal Pension Yojana** (7 crore+ subscribers, guaranteed ₹1,000-5,000 monthly pension), **PM-SYM** for unorganised workers, **PMJJBY (₹2 lakh life cover at ₹436/year)** and **PMSBY (₹2 lakh accident cover at ₹20/year)**. **e-Shram** has 30+ crore registrations and is being linked to scheme delivery. India's social security coverage rose from 19% (2015) to **~49% of the population** — the second largest expansion recorded by the ILO.
items.s: ILO World Social Protection Report / MoLE

items.d: **Mission Shakti** with its two sub-schemes — **Sambal** (One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Nari Adalats) and **Samarthya** (creches under Palna, Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, PMMVY). **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** is credited with a rise in the sex ratio at birth in target districts, though its evaluation found most funds went to media advocacy. **Lakhpati Didi**: 3 crore target, over 1 crore achieved.

**PMAY-G**: over **2.7 crore houses** completed, with an additional 2 crore sanctioned to 2029; **PMAY-U 2.0** targets 1 crore urban houses with an interest subsidy and affordable rental housing complexes. **Jal Jeevan Mission**: rural tap connections rose from **3.23 crore (17%) in 2019 to over 15 crore (~80%)** households — one of the sharpest delivery curves in Indian welfare. **Swachh Bharat**: 100% ODF declared 2019, now ODF-Plus.

**National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (2020)** — a shift from **rule-based to role-based** competency development built on the **FRAC (Framework of Roles, Activities and Competencies)** model, with **behavioural, functional and domain** competencies. Institutions: **PM's HR Council** at the apex, a **Capacity Building Commission**, and **Karmayogi Bharat (SPV)** running the **iGOT** platform — over 1 crore registered users and 3 crore course completions.

**Nine pillars** including broadband highways, universal mobile access, e-Kranti, information for all, electronics manufacturing and 'IT for jobs'. Delivery platforms: **UMANG** (2,000+ services), **DigiLocker** (crossing 40 crore users), **e-Office**, **GeM** (procurement crossing ₹5 lakh crore annual GMV), **NGDRS**, **e-Courts Phase III (₹7,210 crore)** and **BharatNet**, which has connected over 2 lakh gram panchayats with optical fibre.

**CPGRAMS** for grievances (disposal time down to ~13 days), **RTI**, **Citizens' Charters**, the **Sevottam** service-delivery model, **Good Governance Index** (2021, DARPG, 10 sectors and 58 indicators), the **National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment**, and **Special Campaigns for institutionalised swachhata and disposal of pendency**, which have cleared crores of files and freed lakhs of square feet of office space.

**112 districts** and **500 blocks** ranked in real time on **49 indicators across 5 themes** (health and nutrition 30%, education 30%, agriculture and water 20%, financial inclusion and skill 10%, infrastructure 10%). Design principle: **convergence, collaboration and competition**, with a central Prabhari Officer and a district collector-led delta ranking. UNDP's independent assessment called it a model of local area development.

items.t: PM Gati Shakti and the reform of process
items.d: The **National Master Plan** — a GIS platform integrating **44 central ministries and 36 states/UTs** with 1,600+ data layers for infrastructure planning; **National Logistics Policy (2022)** with ULIP; and **Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023**, which **decriminalised 183 provisions across 42 central Acts** to reduce compliance burden. Jan Vishwas 2.0 continues the exercise.

groups.g: Federal transfers and the scheme architecture

items.d: Rationalised to **75 CSS** in three categories — **Core of the Core (6, including MGNREGA and the umbrella scheme for SC/ST/minorities), Core, and Optional**. Typical sharing: **60:40** for most states, **90:10** for the eight North-Eastern and three Himalayan states, and 100% for UTs. States' complaint: **CSS design ties untied funds and distorts state priorities**, and the single nodal agency system tightened flow control.

items.t: Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment
items.d: **₹1.5 lakh crore of 50-year interest-free loans** to states for capex in FY26, with parts of it linked to reforms — scrapping policy, urban planning reforms, and the unbundling of power distribution. The main instrument through which the Centre now shapes state capital spending.

**1,200+ schemes** across 50+ ministries; cumulative **estimated savings of ₹3.48 lakh crore** from removal of duplicate, fake and ineligible beneficiaries. Architecture: **JAM trinity + Public Financial Management System (PFMS) + Aadhaar Payment Bridge**. The critique: exclusion errors from authentication failure, and the shift from universal in-kind to targeted cash.

sections.h: Data for GS-2 — Governance, Justice, Social Sector

items.d: The Lok Sabha now sits for about **55-70 days a year**, against **~130 days in the 1950s**; the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution recommended a **minimum of 100 days for the Lok Sabha and 60 for the Rajya Sabha**. Several state assemblies sit for **under 30 days**.

Only about **16% of bills** introduced in the 17th Lok Sabha were referred to committees, against **60%+ in the 15th**. A significant share of bills are passed **within a day of introduction**, and time spent on the budget's demands for grants has fallen — the empirical basis of the 'decline of Parliament' argument.

**46% of MPs in the 18th Lok Sabha have declared criminal cases**, and about **31% face serious charges** (offences punishable by 5+ years). The figure has risen at every election since 2004 (24% → 30% → 34% → 43% → 46%). ADR data is the standard citation.

Women are about **14% of the Lok Sabha** and under **10% of most state assemblies** — against the global average of ~27% (IPU). The **106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023)** reserves **one-third of seats** in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies and the Delhi assembly, but only **after the census and delimitation**, with a 15-year duration.

Ordinance-making has continued at a steady pace; disruptions cost Parliament a substantial share of scheduled hours, and **question hour is the first casualty**. Productivity of a session is now routinely reported as a percentage of scheduled time — a metric that did not exist before the 2000s.

**~5.29 crore cases pending** — about **4.6 crore in district courts**, **63 lakh in High Courts** and **~86,000 in the Supreme Court**. Over **1.1 crore cases have been pending for more than five years**. The NJDG makes this live and public — itself a transparency reform worth citing.

About **21 judges per million population** against the **50 per million recommended by the Law Commission's 120th Report (1987)** and reiterated in *All India Judges Association*. **Vacancy: ~30% in High Courts** (sanctioned 1,122) and ~20% in the subordinate judiciary. The Supreme Court's sanctioned strength is **34**.

Of the judges appointed to the higher judiciary since 2018, a large majority are from the general category; women are about **10-14% of High Court judges** and there have been only **11 women judges in the Supreme Court's history**. The collegium's own resolutions now cite diversity as a criterion.
items.s: Department of Justice / Rajya Sabha replies

items.d: **Occupancy rate 131%**, and **75.8% of prisoners are undertrials** — one of the highest shares in the world. A disproportionate share of undertrials are SC, ST and OBC and over two-thirds have not completed schooling. **Section 479 BNSS** now allows release of first-time undertrials who have served **one-third** of the maximum sentence.

Under the **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**, about **80% of the population is eligible for free legal aid**, but only a small fraction has ever used it. **Lok Adalats** dispose of crores of cases — the National Lok Adalat settles more cases in a day than courts do in months — but mostly pre-litigation and compoundable matters.

India spends roughly **0.08-0.1% of GDP on the judiciary** — among the lowest of major democracies; most states spend under 1% of their budget on the judiciary. The **All India Judicial Service**, proposed since the 1958 Law Commission's 14th Report and enabled by **Article 312**, remains unimplemented for want of state consensus.

**45-60 lakh RTI applications** are filed a year — among the highest volumes in the world. But **vacancies in Information Commissions** (the Central Information Commission has frequently functioned below strength, and some state commissions have gone defunct) and a backlog of over 4 lakh appeals have blunted it, as documented by the Satark Nagrik Sangathan report cards.

The **first Lokpal was appointed in 2019**, six years after the Act. Complaint numbers are small and prosecution sanctions rarer — the institutional-design-versus-outcome gap. Several states still lack a functioning Lokayukta despite the Act's one-year mandate.

India has roughly **1,600 central government employees per lakh population** — a **small** state by international comparison (the US federal figure is ~4 times higher), contradicting the 'bloated bureaucracy' claim. **IAS: sanctioned ~6,858, in position ~5,500**, a shortfall of over 1,300, with the direct-recruitment intake of 180 a year unable to close it (Baswan Committee, 2016).

Introduced from 2018 on the **Second ARC and NITI Aayog's** recommendation — Joint Secretary, Director and Deputy Secretary posts filled by contract from the private sector, academia and PSUs. Roughly **60+ appointments** so far. The 2024 advertisement was withdrawn over the absence of **reservation** in single-post recruitment — the live controversy.

**CPGRAMS** receives **20+ lakh grievances a year** with average disposal down from 28 to about **13 days**, and now runs an independent feedback call centre. Over **20 states** have Public Service Guarantee Acts with penalties for delay — the enforceable version of the citizens' charter.

groups.g: Local government and federal fiscal facts

items.d: **2.55 lakh gram panchayats** and about **31 lakh elected representatives**, of whom **~46% are women** — well above the one-third mandate, since 21 states legislated 50%. But panchayats raise only about **1% of their revenue on their own** and depend on tied transfers; **only 20 of 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects** are devolved on average, and functionaries rarely follow functions.
items.s: Ministry of Panchayati Raj / RBI Study, 2024

items.d: Municipal own revenue is about **0.15% of GDP** against 2-8% in comparable countries; municipalities' total revenue is ~1% of GDP. Property tax collection is a fraction of potential. **Over 1,400 vacancies of elected councils** and delayed municipal elections in several states defeat Article 243U — the 74th Amendment's weakest limb.

Constitutionally mandated every five years under **Articles 243I and 243Y**, but many states have delayed constitution or failed to table the **Action Taken Report**. The 15th FC made the tabling of the SFC report a **condition for local body grants** from 2024-25 — a rare use of conditionality to enforce a constitutional duty.

States account for about **60% of total government expenditure** but raise only about **35-40% of revenue** — the classic **vertical fiscal imbalance**. Cesses and surcharges, which are **outside the divisible pool**, have risen to a substantial share of the Centre's gross tax revenue, reducing effective devolution below the headline 41%.
items.s: RBI State Finances: A Study of Budgets

items.d: India has an estimated **31 lakh NGOs** (CBI's affidavit to the Supreme Court) — roughly one for every 400 citizens, more than the number of schools or health facilities. About **1.6 lakh** are registered on the **NGO Darpan** portal, and FCRA-registered associations have fallen from over 22,000 to about **16,000** after cancellations and lapses.

Annual foreign contribution receipts by FCRA associations run to roughly **₹15,000-20,000 crore**. The 2020 amendment's ban on **sub-granting** hit the intermediary-grassroots model hardest, since large NGOs traditionally passed funds down to small local organisations.

**~90 lakh SHGs with 10 crore women** under DAY-NRLM, with cumulative bank credit of over **₹10 lakh crore** and NPAs of around **2%** — better than most priority-sector lending. The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, started by **NABARD in 1992**, is the world's largest microfinance programme.
items.s: NABARD Status of Microfinance in India / MoRD

items.d: **Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013** made India the **first country to mandate CSR** — 2% of average net profits of the last three years for companies meeting the turnover, net worth or profit thresholds, with 'comply or explain' converted into a **penalty** in 2021. Annual CSR spending is around **₹30,000 crore**, but is concentrated in a few states and in education and health.

**Land Boundary Agreement, 2015 (100th Amendment)** exchanged 111 enclaves for 51 — the model of a peacefully settled boundary; **Ganga Waters Treaty, 1996** expires in **2026** and its renewal is the live issue; **Teesta** remains unresolved over West Bengal's objection, illustrating the federal constraint on foreign policy. India's largest South Asian trade partner; connectivity through Akhaura-Agartala rail and the Maitri Setu. Relations recalibrated after the political change of 2024.

**Treaty of Peace and Friendship, 1950** — the open border and national-treatment provisions Nepal seeks to revise; the **Eminent Persons Group** report remains unreceived. Friction over **Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura** and Nepal's 2020 map amendment. Cooperation: **power trade** (Nepal now exports surplus hydro to India and, via India, to Bangladesh — a trilateral first), Pancheshwar, and the Motihari-Amlekhganj petroleum pipeline, South Asia's first cross-border oil pipeline.

India's **$4 billion assistance during the 2022 economic crisis** — the largest by any country, and the credibility anchor of the 'first responder' role. Live issues: **13th Amendment** and devolution to Tamil-majority provinces, the **fishermen and Katchatheevu** question, and Chinese research vessels at Hambantota. New: **UPI acceptance, grid connectivity and a multi-product petroleum pipeline** under discussion.

The '**India Out**' turn in 2023-24 and the withdrawal of Indian military personnel operating the aircraft, followed by stabilisation — India remained the **largest bilateral development partner**, extended currency-swap support, and delivered the **Greater Malé Connectivity Project**, the largest infrastructure project in the Maldives. Illustrates the cycle of debt distress, external balancing and return to India.

The closest partnership — **India funds the bulk of Bhutan's Five Year Plan outlay**, and **hydropower (Chukha, Tala, Punatsangchhu, Mangdechhu)** exports to India are the mainstay of Bhutan's revenue. **Doklam (2017)** — a 73-day standoff at a tri-junction on Bhutanese territory — is the standing example of India's security commitment. Bhutan and China are negotiating a boundary settlement, which India watches closely.

**Indus Waters Treaty, 1960**, brokered by the World Bank, gave India the eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) and Pakistan the western (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab), with India entitled to limited non-consumptive use — India has sought **modification of the treaty** and, after the **Pahalgam attack (April 2025)** and **Operation Sindoor**, placed it **in abeyance**. Trade is suspended since 2019; **SAARC is effectively frozen** because of it.

**Line of Actual Control** disputes — **Galwan (June 2020)**, the first fatal clash since 1975; disengagement completed at friction points and **patrolling arrangements at Depsang and Demchok agreed in October 2024**. Trade: bilateral trade over **$127 billion** with a deficit exceeding **$99 billion** — India's largest with any country. Frameworks: the 1993, 1996 and 2005 border agreements, the Special Representatives mechanism (now in its 23rd round), and the WMCC.

items.t: Myanmar and the Act East corridor
items.d: **Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project** (Kolkata-Sittwe-Paletwa-Mizoram) and the **India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway** — both delayed by the post-2021 conflict. India ended the **Free Movement Regime** along the 1,643 km border and is fencing it — a decision contested by Mizoram and Nagaland on ethnic-kinship grounds. Myanmar is the land bridge to ASEAN and the pivot of Act East.

India's development footprint — the **Salma (India-Afghanistan Friendship) Dam**, the **Parliament building**, the Zaranj-Delaram highway — plus wheat and medical assistance after 2021 through a **technical mission in Kabul**. Access runs through **Chabahar**, for which India signed a **10-year port operations contract in 2024**.

**India, US, Japan, Australia** — revived 2017, elevated to leaders' level in 2021. Explicitly a **non-military grouping** for a 'free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific'; working groups on vaccines, critical and emerging technology, climate, infrastructure, space, cyber and maritime domain awareness (**IPMDA**). Note the distinction from **Malabar**, which is the naval exercise (now with the same four members).

Expanded from five to include **Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the UAE** (2024) and further partners since — now representing about **45% of world population** and over 35% of global GDP by PPP. Institutions: the **New Development Bank** (Shanghai, headed by Dilma Rousseff, with India's Kundapur Vaman Kamath as first President) and the **Contingent Reserve Arrangement ($100 bn)**. India's position: BRICS is **non-Western, not anti-Western**, and India has not backed de-dollarisation.

**Shanghai Cooperation Organisation** — India and Pakistan joined in **2017**, Iran in 2023; it is the largest regional organisation by area and population. India uses **RATS (Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure)** and connectivity, but has declined to endorse the **Belt and Road Initiative** in every joint statement — the standing exception recorded in SCO documents.

items.t: G20 and the New Delhi Declaration (2023)
items.d: India's presidency delivered a **consensus leaders' declaration** despite the Ukraine divide, secured **permanent membership for the African Union**, and put **Digital Public Infrastructure**, LiFE, women-led development and multilateral development bank reform on the agenda. Theme: **Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future**. The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** was announced on its margins.

**SAARC (1985, 8 members, Kathmandu secretariat)** — paralysed since 2016 by the unanimity rule and India-Pakistan tension. **BIMSTEC (1997, 7 members, Dhaka secretariat, Charter adopted 2022)** — the working alternative, connecting South and Southeast Asia; India leads the security pillar. **IORA (1997, 23 members)** for the Indian Ocean; **IBSA** (India-Brazil-South Africa); **Colombo Security Conclave** for maritime security.

**I2U2** (India, Israel, UAE, US), **India-France-UAE trilateral**, **Supply Chain Resilience Initiative** (India-Japan-Australia), **Mineral Security Partnership** (India joined 2023), **Artemis Accords** (India signed 2023), **Indo-Pacific Economic Framework** — India joined three of four pillars but **stayed out of the trade pillar**. Also the **International Solar Alliance** (India-France, 120+ signatories, headquartered at Gurugram — the first treaty-based international organisation headquartered in India), the **CDRI**, the **Global Biofuels Alliance** and the **Big Cat Alliance**.

**IMEC** (India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor, 2023) — ship-to-rail across the Gulf to Europe; **INSTC** (International North-South Transport Corridor, 7,200 km via Iran and Russia, cutting transit time to Europe by ~40%); **Chabahar** (Shahid Beheshti terminal, 10-year contract 2024) — India's answer to Gwadar and its access route to Central Asia bypassing Pakistan.

**iCET** (initiative on Critical and Emerging Technology) and its successor framework covering semiconductors, AI, quantum, space and defence co-production; **GE F414 jet engine co-production with HAL (80% ToT)**; **COMCASA (2018)**, **LEMOA (2016)**, **BECA (2020)** and **ISA (2016 General Security of Military Information)** — the four foundational agreements; India designated a **Major Defence Partner (2016)**. Bilateral trade ~$132 bn, the largest; friction over tariffs, immigration and Russian oil.

**Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership** — the only such formulation India uses. Defence dependence has fallen from ~70% to under 40% of imports but remains critical (**S-400**, Su-30MKI, T-90, BrahMos joint venture, nuclear submarine lease). Since 2022, **Russia became India's largest crude supplier**, taking discounted oil to over a third of imports. India's position on Ukraine: **'this is not an era of war'**, abstention at the UN, and calls for dialogue.

**India-EU Trade and Technology Council** (only the EU's second, after the US) and an FTA under negotiation; **India-EFTA TEPA (2024)** — the first agreement in which a partner committed to a **$100 billion investment and 1 million jobs target** over 15 years. **Japan**: the ¥5 trillion investment target, the Mumbai-Ahmedabad **shinkansen**, and the **Act East Forum** for the North-East.

**India-UAE CEPA (2022)** — the first with a Gulf state; **India-Australia ECTA (2022)** with a full CECA under negotiation; **India-EFTA TEPA (2024)**; **India-UK FTA (2025)**. India **withdrew from RCEP in 2019** over the China trade deficit, inadequate safeguards for agriculture and dairy, and rules-of-origin concerns — the single most-asked FTA question.

About **3.5 crore Overseas Indians** — the world's largest diaspora — sending **$129 bn** in remittances. Instruments: **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (9 January**, marking Gandhi's return from South Africa in 1915), **OCI cards**, the Indian Community Welfare Fund, and **Vande Bharat Mission** (evacuating over 60 lakh during COVID) and **Operation Ganga/Kaveri/Ajay** — evacuation diplomacy as a soft-power instrument.

India seeks permanent membership through the **G4 (India, Japan, Germany, Brazil)**, opposed by the **Uniting for Consensus / 'Coffee Club'** (Italy, Pakistan, South Korea, Mexico). The process is stuck in **Intergovernmental Negotiations (IGN)** with no text-based negotiation. India has served **eight terms as a non-permanent member**, most recently 2021-22.

The **Appellate Body has been paralysed since 2019** for want of US appointments, so the dispute settlement system is effectively defunct (with the MPIA as a partial workaround). India's core demands: a **permanent solution on public stockholding for food security** beyond the **Bali Peace Clause (2013)**, **special and differential treatment**, and protection of fisheries subsidies for artisanal fishers. India resists the 'Singapore issues' and the plurilateral route.

India's **updated NDC**: cut **emissions intensity of GDP by 45% from 2005 levels by 2030**, **50% of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030** (achieved in 2025), and **net zero by 2070** — the **Panchamrit** commitments announced at COP26. India champions **CBDR-RC**, climate finance ($100 bn unmet, the **New Collective Quantified Goal** agreed at COP29), and **LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)** as a demand-side idea now in the G20 and UNEP vocabulary.

India is **not a signatory to the NPT or CTBT**, maintains a **No First Use** doctrine with credible minimum deterrence and a triad, and follows a voluntary moratorium on testing. Member of the **MTCR (2016), Wassenaar Arrangement (2017) and Australia Group (2018)** — but **NSG membership is blocked by China** on the NPT-signature ground. The **Indo-US 123 Agreement (2008)** and the **NSG waiver** ended nuclear isolation; the **Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010** and its supplier-liability clause remain the obstacle to reactor imports.

India is the **largest borrower from the World Bank's IBRD/IDA historically** and a founder member of the **AIIB (2016, second-largest shareholder after China)** and the **NDB**. The G20 push for **MDB reform** — 'better, bigger, more effective banks' per the Summers-Singh report — is an Indian priority, along with a **quota realignment at the IMF**, where India's quota share (~2.75%) is far below its GDP share.

**BBNJ 'High Seas' Agreement (2023)** on marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction — India signed in 2024; the **Global Plastics Treaty** negotiations (INC) remain unconcluded; the **WHO Pandemic Agreement (2025)** with its pathogen access and benefit-sharing system; and the **Global Digital Compact** and AI governance debates, where India hosts the **AI Impact Summit in 2026**.

sections.h: Concepts and Vocabulary — Name the Doctrine

items.d: Parliament's amending power under Art. 368 cannot alter the Constitution's identity. Judicially evolved, not textual — the reason India can review amendments while the UK cannot. *Kesavananda* (1973).

**Eclipse**: a pre-Constitution law inconsistent with Part III is not dead but dormant, and revives for non-citizens or if the inconsistency is removed. **Severability**: only the offending part of a statute is struck down if it can be separated (*R.M.D. Chamarbaugwalla*).

'What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly' — a legislature cannot use a subject within its competence as a cover to legislate on one outside it. Tested by **pith and substance**, which asks the true nature and character of the law and tolerates incidental encroachment.

**Article 254** — on a Concurrent List subject, central law prevails, unless the state law received the **President's assent**, and even then Parliament may override it again. The mechanism behind the state farm-law and land-acquisition amendments.

The four-part test from *Puttaswamy* and *Modern Dental College*: **legitimate goal, rational connection, necessity (no less restrictive alternative), and balancing** of the right against the public interest. The default standard for rights adjudication now, replacing bare reasonableness.

A legislative provision can be struck down under **Article 14** if it is capricious, irrational or without adequate determining principle — extended from executive to legislative action in *Shayara Bano* (2017) and applied in *Joseph Shine* and the **Electoral Bonds** judgment.

items.t: Doctrine of pleasure and its limits
items.d: **Article 310** holds civil servants at the pleasure of the President/Governor; **Article 311** limits it with the requirement of an inquiry and a reasonable opportunity, subject to the three exceptions in the second proviso. The Indian version is far more restricted than the English rule.

Fidelity to the Constitution's substantive content — dignity, liberty, equality — over prevailing social morality or majoritarian sentiment. Traced to Grote via Ambedkar, and deployed in *Naz*, *Sabarimala*, *Navtej Johar* and *Joseph Shine*.

The Constitution is read as a document that adapts to changing social realities, and its purpose is not merely to constitute a state but to **transform a hierarchical society into an egalitarian one**. The interpretive philosophy behind the expansion of Article 21.

**Cooperative**: joint action through the GST Council, NITI's Governing Council and the Inter-State Council. **Competitive**: states ranked and made to compete on indices (Ease of Doing Business, SDG India Index, Fiscal Health Index). NITI Aayog's stated model is **'competitive cooperative federalism'**; the critique is that both operate without an institutionalised bargaining forum.

Different states enjoy different constitutional arrangements — **Articles 371 to 371J** for Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra/Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal, Goa and Karnataka, plus the **Fifth and Sixth Schedules** and UT variations. India's federalism is asymmetric by design, not by exception.

A function should be performed at the lowest level of government capable of doing it — the principle underlying the 73rd/74th Amendments and PESA, and explicitly invoked by the **Second ARC** in recommending 'a clear demarcation of functions among the three tiers'.

items.t: New Public Management and New Public Service
items.d: **NPM** — the 1980s doctrine of the citizen as customer, contracting out, performance measurement and the 'steering not rowing' state. **NPS (Denhardt & Denhardt, 2000)** — its corrective: 'serve citizens, not customers; seek the public interest; value citizenship over entrepreneurship'. Both are usable in a governance-reform answer, and the pairing shows depth.

The World Bank's 1992 formulation and the UNESCAP's **eight characteristics**: participatory, consensus-oriented, accountable, transparent, responsive, effective and efficient, equitable and inclusive, and following the rule of law. India's version is the **'minimum government, maximum governance'** and the **SMART** (Simple, Moral, Accountable, Responsive, Transparent) formulation.

**Vertical** (elections, citizen action), **horizontal** (CAG, CVC, judiciary, Parliament), **social** (social audit, RTI, citizen report cards, community scorecards) and **diagonal** (citizens participating in horizontal mechanisms). Naming the type before prescribing a remedy is what lifts a governance answer.

The shift from the state as producer to the state as regulator — SEBI, TRAI, CERC, IRDAI, CCI, PNGRB, RERA, NMC. **Capture** occurs where the regulator advances the interest of the regulated industry; the standard safeguards are **transparency in appointment, tenure security, an appellate tribunal, and funding independent of the regulated**. The **FSLRC** proposed a unified framework for exactly this reason.

items.t: Pressure groups and the Iron Triangle
items.d: Institutional (IAS Association, FICCI), associational (trade unions, farmer organisations), anomic (spontaneous protest) and non-associational. The **'iron triangle'** of the bureaucracy, the legislative committee and the interest group describes policy capture; India's version runs through the **criminal-politician-bureaucrat nexus** identified by the **Vohra Committee**.

**Esping-Andersen's** three worlds — liberal (means-tested, US), conservative-corporatist (status-preserving, Germany) and social-democratic (universal, Nordic). India's is a hybrid: **rights-based statutes (NFSA, MGNREGA, RTE) layered on targeted transfers**, moving from in-kind universalism towards **targeted digital cash** — the JAM turn.

groups.g: The amendments to know by number

items.d: Added **Article 15(4)** and the **Ninth Schedule** after *Champakam Dorairajan*; added 'public order', 'friendly relations with foreign states' and 'incitement to an offence' to the Article 19(2) restrictions.
Gave effect to the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** — abolished the Part A/B/C/D classification and created 14 states and 6 union territories.

**24th** — Parliament's power to amend any part, and the President's obligation to assent to an amendment bill; **25th** — Article 31C and 'amount' replacing 'compensation'; **26th** — abolition of **privy purses**.

The 'mini-Constitution' — added **Socialist, Secular, Integrity** to the Preamble, **Fundamental Duties (51A)**, Articles 39A, 43A, 48A; made the Council's advice binding; extended the Lok Sabha's term to six years; moved education, forests, weights and measures, and wildlife to the **Concurrent List**.

The Janata government's reversal — **right to property moved to Article 300A**; 'internal disturbance' in Article 352 replaced by **'armed rebellion'**; **Articles 20 and 21 non-suspendable** in an emergency; the Cabinet's written advice required for a proclamation; term restored to five years.

**52nd** — the **Tenth Schedule** on defection; **91st** — deleted the one-third split exception (leaving only a two-thirds **merger**), and capped the Council of Ministers at **15% of the House** (minimum 12 in states).
Reduced the **voting age from 21 to 18** — the single largest expansion of the Indian electorate.

Constitutional status for **panchayats (Part IX, Eleventh Schedule, 29 subjects)** and **municipalities (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule, 18 subjects)**, with SECs, SFCs and reservation for women and SC/ST.
**Article 21A** — free and compulsory education for 6-14 as a fundamental right; recast Article 45 as early childhood care; added the parental duty in 51A(k).

**Cooperative societies** — Article 19(1)(c) extended to them, Part IXB added and **Article 43B** as a DPSP. Part IXB was **struck down for state cooperatives in 2021** for want of state ratification, surviving only for multi-state cooperatives.

**GST** — Article 246A (simultaneous power), 269A (inter-state supply), **279A (GST Council)**, and compensation to states for five years. *Mohit Minerals* (2022) held the Council's recommendations **not binding**.

**102nd** — constitutional status for the **NCBC (Art. 338B)** and Articles 342A and 366(26C); read in *Maratha Reservation* (2021) as taking away the states' power to identify SEBCs, which the **105th Amendment restored**.
**10% EWS reservation** through Articles 15(6) and 16(6) — upheld 3:2 in *Janhit Abhiyan* (2022), which held that economic criteria alone are permissible and the 50% ceiling is not inviolable.
Extended **SC/ST reservation in legislatures by ten years** to 2030 and **ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians** to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies.

**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** — one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha, state assemblies and the Delhi assembly reserved for women, **effective only after the census and delimitation**, for 15 years, with rotation of reserved seats.

items.t: Constitutional vs statutory vs executive bodies
items.d: **Constitutional** — ECI, UPSC, CAG, Finance Commission, AG, NCSC/NCST/NCBC, GST Council. **Statutory** — NHRC, CVC, Lokpal, NCW, CIC, NGT, NCPCR. **Executive** — NITI Aayog, CBI (whose only basis is the DSPE Act), NDC (defunct), Central Vigilance Commission before 2003. Getting this classification right is a routine mark.

**Habeas corpus** (produce the body — against the state and private persons), **mandamus** (command a public duty — not against a private person or the President/Governor), **prohibition** (stop a lower court exceeding jurisdiction — before the order), **certiorari** (quash an order — after; now also against administrative bodies), **quo warranto** (by what authority do you hold this public office — open to any person).

**32** is itself a fundamental right, available only for the enforcement of fundamental rights, and the SC cannot refuse; **226** is a constitutional right, available for fundamental rights **and 'any other purpose'**, discretionary, and territorially wider. Hence the High Court's writ jurisdiction is **broader** than the Supreme Court's.

**352 National** (war, external aggression or armed rebellion; approval within one month by both Houses with a **special majority**; six months at a time), **356 State** (approval within two months by simple majority; six months at a time, maximum three years with conditions), **360 Financial** (never used). Under 352, **Article 19 is suspended only in a war/external-aggression emergency**, and 20 and 21 never.

**Money bill (Art. 110)** — only the six specified matters; Lok Sabha only, RS has 14 days and recommendatory power; Speaker certifies. **Financial Bill I (117(1))** — contains money-bill matters plus others; Lok Sabha only but the RS has full power. **Financial Bill II (117(3))** — involves expenditure from the Consolidated Fund; may start in either House.

An amendment bill needs a **special majority** (majority of the total membership **and** two-thirds present and voting) in each House **separately**, with **ratification by half the states** for federal provisions; there is **no joint sitting**, and the President **must** assent (24th Amendment).

items.t: Vote on account vs interim budget
items.d: A **vote on account** is only the grant of funds to carry on until the full budget is passed; an **interim budget** is a complete set of accounts including estimates — presented in an election year by convention without major policy announcements.

The **Speaker** certifies money bills, presides over joint sittings, decides defection cases and has a casting vote; the **Rajya Sabha Chairman (Vice-President)** is not a member of the House. The Speaker's removal requires 14 days' notice and a resolution by **effective majority**, and he does not vacate office on the dissolution of the Lok Sabha.

**Parliamentary sovereignty (UK) vs constitutional supremacy (US) vs India's middle path** — a written Constitution with basic structure, judicial review narrower than US 'due process' but wider than the UK's; a **federal structure with a strong Centre ('quasi-federal' — Wheare; 'federal in form, unitary in spirit')**; and an integrated judiciary unlike the US's dual system.

**UK** — parliamentary system, rule of law, single citizenship, writs, bicameralism; **US** — Fundamental Rights, judicial review, impeachment, independence of the judiciary, preamble; **Ireland** — DPSPs, nomination to the RS, method of the President's election; **Canada** — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Union; **Australia** — Concurrent List, trade and commerce, joint sitting; **Germany** — emergency provisions; **USSR** — Fundamental Duties, justice in the Preamble; **France** — liberty, equality, fraternity; **South Africa** — amendment procedure and election of RS members; **Japan** — procedure established by law.

Record **~354 million tonnes (2024-25)**, up from 332 MT (2023-24) and 252 MT (2014-15). Rice ~149 MT, **wheat ~117.5 MT**, coarse cereals/Shree Anna ~60 MT, **pulses ~25.2 MT**, oilseeds ~41 MT, sugarcane ~450 MT, cotton ~30 million bales. **Horticulture (~355 MT) now exceeds foodgrain output** — the quiet structural shift.

**Net sown area ~140 million ha**, gross cropped ~220 million ha, **cropping intensity ~155%**; forest ~72 million ha; net irrigated area is **~55% of net sown area**, so nearly half of Indian farming is still rainfed. Average operational holding **1.08 ha** and falling; **86% of holdings are small and marginal (<2 ha)** and they operate ~47% of the area.

India is the **world's largest producer (~25% of global output), largest consumer and largest importer**. Production **25.2 MT** on about 28 million ha — the yield is barely 800 kg/ha against a world average above 1,000. Imports ~**6.6 MT**, mainly **yellow peas and lentils from Canada and Russia, tur from Mozambique and Myanmar, urad from Myanmar**. **Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses (2025-26)**: ₹11,440 crore over six years, targeting self-sufficiency in tur, urad and masoor by 2030-31.

India imports **~57% of its edible oil consumption**, ~16 MT worth about **$17 billion** — the **largest single agricultural import** and second only to crude and gold in the import bill. Palm from Indonesia and Malaysia, soy from Argentina and Brazil, sunflower from Russia and Ukraine. **National Mission on Edible Oils - Oil Palm (₹11,040 crore)** and the Oilseeds mission (₹10,103 crore) target 25 MT of domestic oilseed output.

Only about **10% of India's food output is processed** and roughly **2% of fruits and vegetables**, against 65% in the US and 23% in China; post-harvest losses run to about **₹1.53 lakh crore a year**. Food processing is ~7.7% of manufacturing GVA and employs ~20 lakh in the registered sector. **PMKSY (₹6,000 crore)** and **PMFME (₹10,000 crore, 2 lakh micro units)** are the interventions; the **PLI for food processing** is ₹10,900 crore.

India is the **largest milk producer — 239 MT, ~24% of world output** — with **per capita availability ~471 g/day** against the world's 322; the dairy sector contributes ~5% of GVA and supports 8 crore households, mostly landless and small farmers. Fisheries: **~184 lakh tonnes**, second largest producer globally, **largest shrimp exporter**; the sector grew at ~8-9% under **PMMSY (₹20,050 crore)**. Livestock is now ~30% of agricultural GVA and growing faster than crops.
items.s: DAHD Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics / DoF

items.d: Consumption ~**60 million tonnes**; the **NPK ratio is skewed to about 8:3:1 against the ideal 4:2:1**, because urea alone remains under statutory price control while P&K are under NBS. Urea imports ~7 MT and the fertiliser subsidy is **₹1.67 lakh crore (FY26 BE)**. Soil Health Cards issued in crores; **Nano urea and PM-PRANAM** (rewarding states that cut chemical fertiliser use) are the corrective instruments.

MSP is announced for **22 crops plus FRP for sugarcane**, on the CACP's recommendation, and since 2018-19 at **A2+FL plus 50%** — not the **C2+50%** the Swaminathan Commission recommended, which is the core of the farmers' demand. Only about **6% of farmers actually sell at MSP** (Shanta Kumar Committee, 2015), and procurement is concentrated in rice and wheat and in Punjab, Haryana, MP and Chhattisgarh.

Average monthly income of an agricultural household **₹10,218**, of which only ~37% comes from crop production — **wages contribute nearly as much**. Average debt per indebted household ₹74,121, and **50.2% of agricultural households are indebted**. Agricultural credit target ~₹22-25 lakh crore; **KCC** is the main channel, and the **Modified Interest Subvention Scheme** gives crop loans up to ₹3 lakh at an effective 4%.

Agriculture consumes **~78-80% of India's water**; **groundwater supplies ~60% of irrigation and 85% of rural drinking water**, and the national stage of extraction is ~60%, with over-exploited blocks concentrated in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan and western UP. **Micro-irrigation** covers ~1.5 crore ha under PMKSY 'Per Drop More Crop' against a potential of 7 crore ha. Rice and sugarcane take a disproportionate share — the crop-mix problem.
items.s: CGWB Assessment / Ministry of Jal Shakti

items.d: Manufacturing ~**17% of GVA** against the 25% target. **Production Linked Incentive schemes across 14 sectors, outlay ₹1.97 lakh crore** — actual investment realised over ₹1.6 lakh crore, production/sales over ₹14 lakh crore, incremental employment ~12 lakh, and incentives disbursed a fraction of the outlay. **Mobile phones are the standout**: India moved from importing most handsets to **exporting over $20 billion** worth, with Apple's Indian production a large share.

**National Infrastructure Pipeline** — over ₹111 lakh crore of projects; **National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0** for brownfield asset monetisation (roads, transmission, railways, telecom towers). Roads: national highways grew from **91,287 km (2014) to over 1.46 lakh km**, with construction peaking above 30 km/day. Railways: **100% electrification of broad gauge nearly complete**, dedicated freight corridors commissioned, and **Vande Bharat** as the flagship.

India's logistics cost is estimated at **~8-9% of GDP** (NCAER, 2023 study for DPIIT) — lower than the long-quoted '13-14%' figure but still above the global benchmark of ~8%. The **National Logistics Policy (2022)** targets single-digit cost, top-25 LPI rank by 2030, and a unified digital platform (**ULIP**), with **PM Gati Shakti** as the planning backbone.

India handles about **1,600 million tonnes** of cargo across 12 major and 200+ non-major ports; **Vadhavan Port (₹76,000 crore)** is the largest new deep-water project, and **Vizhinjam** is India's first deep-water transhipment port — India previously routed most transhipment through Colombo, Singapore and Salalah. **Sagarmala** and the **Maritime India Vision 2030**/Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 are the frameworks. India's share of global shipbuilding is under 1%.

**Airports: 74 (2014) → 150+**, with **UDAN** connecting unserved airstrips; India is the **3rd largest domestic aviation market**, and Indian carriers hold the largest aircraft order book in the world. **Inland waterways**: 111 National Waterways declared, but cargo movement is concentrated on NW-1 (Ganga), NW-2 (Brahmaputra) and NW-3, and the modal share of waterways remains ~2% against 47% in China.

**GNPA at a multi-decade low of ~2.5%**, down from 11.2% (2018); capital adequacy ~16-17%; the **IBC has resolved cases with a recovery rate of ~31%** of admitted claims but with significant haircuts and delays beyond the 330-day limit. Bank credit growth ~12-15%; **credit-to-GDP ratio ~56%**, well below peer economies — the financial-deepening gap.

Demat accounts crossed **19 crore**; **monthly SIP inflows above ₹26,000 crore** and mutual fund AUM above ₹65 lakh crore — the retailisation of Indian savings. **Financial Inclusion Index (RBI) rose from 43.4 (2017) to ~64.2** — measuring access, usage and quality. Insurance penetration, however, **fell to ~3.7%** against the world's 7% — 'Insurance for All by 2047' is the IRDAI target.

**~484 GW total**, of which **non-fossil crossed 50% in June 2025 — five years ahead of the NDC target**. Solar ~110 GW, wind ~51 GW, large hydro ~47 GW, nuclear ~8.7 GW. But **coal still generates ~70-74% of electricity** because of the capacity-generation gap — always state both numbers together.

**500 GW non-fossil by 2030**; instruments — **PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana** (1 crore rooftop households, ₹75,021 crore), **PM-KUSUM** for solar pumps, **National Green Hydrogen Mission (₹19,744 crore, 5 MMT annual production by 2030)**, PLI for solar modules (~₹24,000 crore), viability gap funding for offshore wind and battery storage, and the **International Solar Alliance**.

Per capita electricity consumption ~**1,395 kWh**, less than half the world average of ~3,500. **Crude import dependence ~88%** and natural gas ~50%; coal imports ~240 MT despite record domestic production above 1 billion tonnes. India is the **third largest energy consumer** and will account for the largest share of global demand growth to 2030.

India is the **3rd largest emitter (~7-8% of global)** with **per capita emissions ~2 tCO₂e against a world average of 4.7**; cumulative historical share under 4%. NDC: **45% cut in emission intensity of GDP by 2030 from 2005** (already achieved ~36% by 2020), **net zero by 2070**. Instruments: the **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme under the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022**, PAT, and the compliance carbon market from 2026.

**Forest and tree cover 25.17%** (forest 21.76% + tree 3.41%) against the **33% policy target**; mangroves 4,992 km². India has **4 of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots**, ~8% of global recorded species on 2.4% of the land. Protected areas: **106 national parks and 573 sanctuaries**, ~5.3% of the area; **tigers 3,682 (75% of the world's wild tigers)**, **Asiatic lions 891 (2025)**, elephants ~30,000, and **91 Ramsar sites**.

**Municipal solid waste ~1.7 lakh tonnes/day**, ~91% collected but only about **54% processed**; **e-waste 1.75 MT a year with ~43% recycled**; plastic waste ~41 lakh TPA. **Sewage: generation ~72,000 MLD against treatment capacity ~31,800 MLD**, so over half of urban sewage is untreated — the single most citable number for river pollution. **39 of the world's 50 most polluted cities** are in India.

**~59% of India's landmass is earthquake-prone**, **~12% flood-prone (40 million ha)**, **~5,700 km of the 7,516 km coastline is cyclone- and tsunami-prone**, and **~68% of cultivable land is drought-prone**. India ranks among the countries with the highest absolute disaster losses; economic losses run to tens of billions of dollars a decade. **NDRF ~₹1.6 lakh crore for 2021-26** under the 15th FC's mitigation-plus-response architecture.

India's **gross expenditure on R&D is ~0.64-0.7% of GDP**, against China's ~2.4%, the US's ~3.5% and Israel and Korea above 4.5%. Uniquely, **the government funds ~55-60%** of Indian R&D while business funds most of it elsewhere — the structural weakness the **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (₹50,000 crore, 70% from private sources)** is meant to correct. Researchers per million: ~250 against a world average above 1,500.

Patent filings crossed **90,000 a year**, with **residents filing the majority for the first time**; grants rose about 10x in a decade and the examination backlog fell sharply. India is the **3rd largest producer of scientific publications**, but citations per paper and the share of high-impact work lag.
items.s: Indian Patent Office / NSF Science & Engineering Indicators

items.d: Space economy ~**$8.4 bn (2%)** targeted at **$44 bn by 2033**; **100% FDI liberalised (2024)** with automatic route up to 74% for satellites; 300+ startups (Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Dhruva). Milestones: **Chandrayaan-3 (first landing at the lunar south pole, 2023)**, Aditya-L1 at L1, **SpaDeX docking (2025)**, **NISAR with NASA (2025)**, Shubhanshu Shukla on Axiom-4. Targets: **Bharatiya Antariksh Station 2035, crewed lunar landing 2040**, Gaganyaan crewed flight.

**India Semiconductor Mission — ₹76,000 crore**; approved units at Dholera (Tata-PSMC fab), Sanand (Micron ATMP, CG Power, Kaynes), Morigaon (Tata OSAT) and Jewar; **the first indigenously packaged chip in 2025**. Electronics production crossed **$115 billion** and mobile exports over $20 billion — but **value addition is only ~20%**, since most of it is assembly. The **Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (₹22,919 crore)** targets exactly this.

**IndiaAI Mission ₹10,372 crore** with 38,000+ GPUs empanelled, AIKosh datasets and safety institutes; India is **1st in AI skill penetration** (Stanford AI Index) and among the top contributors on GitHub AI projects, but private AI investment is a small fraction of the US and China. India hosts the **AI Impact Summit in 2026**. **National Quantum Mission — ₹6,003 crore**, targeting 50-1,000 physical qubit machines within eight years.

Defence budget **₹6.81 lakh crore (FY26)**, ~13% of the union budget; **domestic production a record ~₹1.51 lakh crore** and **exports ₹23,622 crore, up from ₹686 crore in 2013-14 — a 34-fold rise**; exports now go to 100+ countries. Instruments: **75% of the capital procurement budget reserved for domestic industry**, five **positive indigenisation lists**, **iDEX** for startups, DAP 2020, and corporatisation of the Ordnance Factory Board into 7 DPSUs. India remains among the top 2 arms importers globally — hold both facts together.

**Left-Wing Extremism**: districts affected down from **126 (2010) to 38 (2024)**, with 'most affected' down to 6-18; violence down over 70% and the government's target is to end LWE by **31 March 2026**. **J&K**: terror incidents down sharply since 2019; **North-East**: AFSPA withdrawn from large parts of Assam, Manipur, Nagaland and Arunachal, and multiple accords signed (Bodo 2020, Karbi Anglong 2021, Adivasi 2022, ULFA 2023). **Cybercrime**: 65,893 cases (NCRB 2022, +24.4%) and **over 22 lakh complaints a year on the NCRP**, with the **I4C** as the nodal body.

**Target**: all landholding farmer families. **Design**: ₹6,000 a year in three instalments, DBT to the Aadhaar-seeded account, with land-record and e-KYC verification. **Numbers**: about **9.8 crore beneficiaries** and over **₹3.7 lakh crore** disbursed since 2019 — the largest income-support programme in the world by beneficiary count. **Gap**: tenant farmers and landless cultivators are excluded because the trigger is land title.

items.t: PMFBY — Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
items.d: Premium capped at **2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi) and 5% (commercial/horticultural)** with the balance shared by the Centre and state; **voluntary since 2020**. Around 4 crore farmer applications annually; claims paid over ₹1.7 lakh crore against premiums of about ₹35,000 crore paid by farmers. Uses **YES-TECH and WINDS** for yield estimation and weather data, cutting the crop-cutting-experiment delay. Several states exited over the state-share burden.

**Electronic National Agriculture Market** — 1,400+ mandis across 23 states integrated, 1.8 crore farmers and 2.5 lakh traders registered, with assaying, e-payment and inter-mandi trade. The binding constraint is that **APMC is a state subject**: e-NAM cannot create a single national market by itself, which is what the repealed 2020 farm laws attempted.

**₹1 lakh crore** of medium-to-long term debt financing for post-harvest infrastructure — with a **3% interest subvention and credit guarantee up to ₹2 crore**; over ₹50,000 crore sanctioned across 1 lakh+ projects. Complements the **10,000 FPO scheme (₹6,865 crore)** and the world's largest **decentralised grain storage plan** in the cooperative sector.

**National Mission on Natural Farming (₹2,481 crore)** targeting 1 crore farmers and 7.5 lakh ha in 15,000 clusters, with Bhartiya Prakritik Kheti Bio-input Resource Centres. Andhra Pradesh's **Community-Managed Natural Farming** is the flagship state model, and Sikkim is the **world's first fully organic state (2016)**. Counterpoint for balance: Sri Lanka's abrupt 2021 organic switch and the resulting yield collapse.

Announced in Budget 2025-26 — convergence of **36 existing schemes across 11 ministries** in **100 low-productivity districts**, covering 1.7 crore farmers, on the Aspirational Districts template: measure, rank, converge. The agricultural counterpart of the ADP.

**MGNREGA** — ~₹86,000 crore a year, 5-6 crore households employed, average days worked per household ~50 against the 100 guaranteed; being restructured as **VB-G RAM G**. **PMGSY** — 7.6 lakh km of rural roads connecting 99%+ of eligible habitations; **DAY-NRLM** for SHGs; **SVAMITVA** for property cards.

**14 sectors, ₹1.97 lakh crore**: mobiles and electronics, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, automobiles, ACC batteries, textiles, food processing, white goods, solar modules, drones, telecom, speciality steel. Design: incentive on **incremental** sales over a base year, paid only on achieved investment and production — output-linked, not input-subsidy. Mobile manufacturing is the success case; some sectors have underperformed on disbursal.

The **investment-and-turnover definition** (revised upward in Budget 2025-26: micro ₹2.5 cr/₹10 cr, small ₹25 cr/₹100 cr, medium ₹125 cr/₹500 cr) removed the disincentive to grow. **CGTMSE** guarantee cover expanded to ₹10 crore; **TReDS** for receivables discounting; the **45-day payment rule** under Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act; **PM Vishwakarma (₹13,000 crore)** for 18 traditional trades; **PM SVANidhi** for street vendors.

**ELI scheme (₹99,446 crore)** from Budget 2024-25, targeting **3.5 crore jobs over two years** through three parts: **Scheme A** — one month's EPF wage (up to ₹15,000) to first-timers; **Scheme B** — support to employers and employees in manufacturing; **Scheme C** — reimbursement of employers' EPFO contribution up to ₹3,000 a month. The first large-scale Indian attempt at a **wage-subsidy approach to formalisation**.

**Four codes consolidating 29 laws** — **Code on Wages (2019)** with a statutory national floor wage and universal minimum wage; **Industrial Relations Code (2020)** raising the retrenchment threshold to **300 workers** and requiring 60-day strike notice; **Social Security Code (2020)** extending cover to **gig and platform workers** with an aggregator contribution of 1-2% of turnover; **OSH Code (2020)**. Notified but implementation awaited pending state rules — the largest pending labour reform.

**Startup India** — tax holiday for three years under 80-IAC, **Fund of Funds ₹10,000 crore** through SIDBI, **Startup India Seed Fund ₹945 crore**, self-certification and faster exit. **Atal Innovation Mission** — 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs and Atal Incubation Centres. **1.6 lakh+ recognised startups, 100+ unicorns, 3rd largest ecosystem**, with ~45% from tier-2/3 cities.

items.t: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
items.d: **₹75,021 crore** to install rooftop solar on **1 crore households**, with up to **300 units of free electricity a month**, a central subsidy of up to ₹78,000, collateral-free loans at ~7%, and a model solar village per district. The largest domestic rooftop programme in the world by target.

**₹19,744 crore** — target **5 MMT of annual green hydrogen production by 2030** with 125 GW of associated renewable capacity, ₹8 lakh crore of investment and 6 lakh jobs; **SIGHT** programme incentivises electrolyser manufacturing and hydrogen production. India aims to be a **global hub for production and export**, with green ammonia for fertiliser and shipping as the near-term markets.

The **Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023**, framed under the **Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act, 2022** — a **compliance mechanism** with intensity targets for obligated entities from 2026, plus an offset mechanism for non-obligated entities, administered by BEE with the Grid Controller as registry. Succeeds the **PAT (Perform, Achieve and Trade)** scheme and the REC market.

**Lifestyle for Environment** — launched at COP26 and carried into the **G20 New Delhi Declaration**, shifting from 'mindless consumption' to 'mindful utilisation'; the demand-side complement to supply-side decarbonisation. **Circular economy**: EPR regimes for plastic, e-waste, battery and tyre waste; **Vehicle Scrappage Policy**; the ban on identified single-use plastics (2022); and **GOBARdhan** for waste-to-energy.

**Jal Jeevan Mission** — rural tap connections from **3.23 crore (17%) in 2019 to over 15 crore (~80%)**. **Atal Bhujal Yojana** — ₹6,000 crore in 7 states with community water security plans as the condition for incentives. **Namami Gange (₹20,000 crore+)** and the **Arth Ganga** livelihood model. **Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain**; and the **National River Linking Project**, whose first link is **Ken-Betwa (₹44,605 crore)**.

**DM Act, 2005** with NDMA (PM-chaired), SDMA, DDMA, NDRF (16 battalions) and NIDM. The **DM (Amendment) Act, 2025** gives statutory status to the **National Crisis Management Committee and the High Level Committee**, empowers NDMA to prepare the national plan itself and create an **Urban Disaster Management Authority** for state capitals and large cities. Funds: **NDRF/SDRF plus dedicated mitigation funds (NDMF/SDMF)** on the 15th FC's recommendation.

**NQM — ₹6,003 crore (2023-31)**: intermediate-scale quantum computers of 50-1,000 physical qubits, satellite-based secure quantum communication over 2,000 km, and four thematic hubs. **Anusandhan National Research Foundation (₹50,000 crore, of which ₹36,000 crore is to come from private and philanthropic sources)** — created by the ANRF Act, 2023, replacing SERB, with the PM as ex-officio President.

**UPI** (18-19 bn transactions/month, ~half of global real-time payments), **Aadhaar Enabled Payment System**, **Account Aggregator** framework for consent-based data sharing, **ONDC** to unbundle e-commerce, **OCEN** for cash-flow-based lending, **e-RUPI** vouchers, and the **e-Rupee CBDC** pilots in retail and wholesale. Together these are what India exports as **Digital Public Infrastructure**.

**I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre)** with the **National Cybercrime Reporting Portal** (22+ lakh complaints a year), the **Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System** and its 1930 helpline, **CERT-In** as the nodal agency under the IT Act (with the 2022 directions on 6-hour incident reporting), **NCIIPC** for critical information infrastructure, and the **National Cyber Security Policy 2013** — long overdue for replacement.

**PMLA, 2002** — ED as the investigating agency, with the **twin conditions for bail under Section 45** upheld in *Vijay Madanlal Choudhary* (2022); **FIU-IND** for financial intelligence. India's **FATF Mutual Evaluation (2024)** placed it in the **'regular follow-up' category — the highest tier, achieved by only a handful of countries** — while flagging delays in prosecution and the need to supervise non-financial sectors.

**NIA** under the NIA Act, 2008 (post-26/11), with extraterritorial jurisdiction after the 2019 amendment; **NATGRID** linking 11 agencies to 21 databases; **MAC (Multi Agency Centre)** for intelligence sharing; **CCTNS** and the **Interoperable Criminal Justice System**; **NSG, CAPFs (~10 lakh personnel)**, and the **Chief of Defence Staff and Department of Military Affairs (2019)** with theatre commands under consideration. **Agnipath (2022)** for military recruitment.

sections.h: Case Law for GS-3 — Environment, Economy, Security

items.t: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak, 1987)
items.d: Laid down **absolute liability** — an enterprise in a hazardous activity is **absolutely and non-delegably liable** for harm, with **no exceptions** to the rule in *Rylands v. Fletcher*, and damages must be **correlated to the magnitude and capacity of the enterprise** so as to deter. India's own contribution to environmental tort law.

Bichhri case — applied **absolute liability plus the Polluter Pays Principle**, holding that the polluter must bear the cost of both compensation and **restoring the degraded environment**. Established that PPP is part of Indian environmental law without needing a statute.

Tamil Nadu tanneries case — held that the **Precautionary Principle and the Polluter Pays Principle are part of the law of the land** as customary international law read into Articles 21, 47, 48A and 51A(g), and that **sustainable development is a balancing concept**, not a bar on development.

The 'continuing mandamus' that redefined **'forest' in its dictionary sense**, irrespective of ownership or notification, bringing all such land under the Forest (Conservation) Act; created the **CEC** and the **CAMPA** compensatory-afforestation regime with **Net Present Value** payments. The longest-running environmental case in the world. The **Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 2023** narrowed this definition — and was read down by the Court in 2024 to restore the *Godavarman* meaning for identification purposes.

**The first environmental PIL** in India — ordered the closure of limestone quarries in the Mussoorie hills, holding that the **right to a wholesome environment is part of Article 21** and that ecological balance may override economic loss.

'**Right to life includes the right of enjoyment of pollution-free water and air**' — the clearest single-line authority for the environmental content of Article 21, though the Court also warned that PIL must not be used for personal or oblique motives.

Held that the **gram sabha must decide** whether bauxite mining would affect the **religious and cultural rights of the Dongria Kondh** under the Forest Rights Act and PESA — all twelve gram sabhas voted against. The strongest Indian authority for **community consent in resource decisions**.

Great Indian Bustard: recognised the **right against the adverse effects of climate change** under Articles 14 and 21, read with Articles 48A and 51A(g); balanced species protection against solar transmission infrastructure by replacing a blanket ban on overhead lines with an expert-committee assessment. India's first constitutional climate-rights judgment.

*Alembic* held that **ex post facto environmental clearance is contrary to law** and 'in derogation of the fundamental principles of environmental jurisprudence', although it declined to demolish operating plants. *Common Cause* (mining) applied the public trust doctrine to natural-resource allocation and ordered recovery from illegal mining.

items.t: Paryavaran Suraksha Samiti (2017) and Almitra Patel (2000)
items.d: *Paryavaran Suraksha Samiti* directed every local body to set up **sewage treatment plants** with timelines and made the state liable for untreated sewage. *Almitra Patel* produced the **Municipal Solid Waste Rules** and the direction against open dumping — the basis of the SWM Rules, 2016.

Mopa airport, Goa — suspended the environmental clearance for **non-disclosure and inadequate EIA**, holding that the process must be rigorous and that **'the rule of law is not merely a rule of procedure'** in environmental governance. The leading case on EIA integrity.

Upheld the **PMLA** framework — ED's powers of arrest, search and attachment, the **reverse burden of proof under Section 24**, the non-supply of the ECIR, and the **twin conditions for bail in Section 45**. Review is pending; the Court has since read in safeguards on written grounds of arrest (*Pankaj Bansal*, 2023, and *Arvind Kejriwal*, 2024).

**GST Council recommendations are recommendatory, not binding** — Parliament and state legislatures have simultaneous power under Article 246A; the Court described Indian federalism as involving **dialogue between cooperative and uncooperative federalism**. The single most cited GST judgment.

Nine judges, 8:1 — **royalty is not a tax**, and **states have independent power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land**; overruled *India Cement* (1990). Applied prospectively from 1 April 2005. A landmark for state fiscal capacity in mineral-rich states.

items.t: Property Owners' Association v. State of Maharashtra (2024)
items.d: Nine judges: **not every privately owned resource is a 'material resource of the community' under Article 39(b)** — overruled the expansive view in *Ranganatha Reddy* and *Sanjeev Coke*, and rejected the idea that the Constitution mandates a particular economic ideology. The definitive statement of constitutional economic neutrality.

items.t: Centre for PIL v. Union of India (2G, 2012)
items.d: Cancelled **122 telecom licences** allotted on a first-come-first-served basis, holding that natural resources must be alienated through a **transparent method**, generally auction — later clarified in the **Presidential Reference (2012)** that **auction is not a constitutional mandate for all resources**, only that the method must be fair and maximise public good.

Cancelled **204 of 218 coal block allocations** made since 1993 as arbitrary and illegal, and levied a charge per tonne extracted. Led directly to the **Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015** and to competitive auctioning of coal blocks and commercial mining.
